findings.name: Homestead Exemption for Disabled Veterans
findings.description: Ohio veterans with a total (100%) VA service-connected disability rating, or compensated at the 100% rate based on individual unemployability, may exempt $50,000 of their home's true (market) value from local property taxation, with no income test applied (unlike the standard senior/disabled-civilian homestead track). Some secondary sources report the dollar figure has been adjusted upward for inflation in recent tax years, but this research could not directly confirm a current-year adjusted figure from an accessible official page, so only the statutory base amount is reported here.
findings.value: $50,000 of true value exempted from property taxation (statutory base amount, adjusted annually for inflation per ORC 323.152(A)(1)(d))
otherReqs: Own and occupy the home as principal place of residence
No income test applied to the veteran's disability-based homestead track
File application with the county auditor by December 31 of the year the exemption is sought
findings.agency: County Auditor (program administered under Ohio Department of Taxation rules)
documentation: VA award letter or determination letter showing 100% disability rating (or 100% individual unemployability compensation)
findings.sourceExcerpt: the product obtained by multiplying fifty thousand dollars of the true value of the property in money, as adjusted under division (A)(1)(d) of this section, by the amounts described in divisions (A)(1)(c)(ii) to (iv) of this section

findings.name: Ohio Veterans Homes (Sandusky & Georgetown)
findings.description: Ohio operates two state veterans homes, in Sandusky (domiciliary and nursing care) and Georgetown (nursing home with standard and memory care), for eligible Ohio veterans who have a disability that leaves them incapable of self-support. This research could not directly confirm the department's current eligibility wording because dvs.ohio.gov blocked automated page retrieval during every attempt; details below are drawn from cross-referenced secondary sources and should be independently re-verified before being presented as fact to a veteran.
otherReqs: Ohio residency (commonly cited as at least one year, not independently confirmed)
Honorable discharge or separation under honorable conditions
Wartime/qualifying service era or receipt of the Armed Forces Expeditionary Medal/Vietnam Service Medal (per secondary sources, not independently confirmed)
Disability that renders the veteran incapable of self-support

findings.name: Ohio War Orphan & Severely Disabled Veterans' Children Scholarship (WOS)
findings.description: Undergraduate tuition assistance for the children of Ohio veterans who died of service-connected causes, are POW/MIA, or have a 60%-or-greater service-connected disability (or receive VA benefits for permanent and total non-service-connected disability). Covers a portion of instructional and general fee charges at eligible Ohio public and private colleges; the exact current award percentage or dollar cap could not be confirmed from an official page this research could directly access, so it is intentionally omitted rather than guessed.
findings.value: Partial tuition/general-fee coverage at eligible Ohio public and private institutions (exact current percentage or dollar cap not confirmed from an accessible official page)
otherReqs: Child (natural, adopted, or qualifying stepchild) of a qualifying Ohio veteran
Full-time undergraduate enrollment pursuing an associate or bachelor's degree at an eligible Ohio institution
Apply by May 15 each year
Applicant age window of 16-24 is widely cited in program application materials but was not independently re-confirmed by direct fetch in this research
findings.agency: Ohio Department of Higher Education / Ohio War Orphans and Severely Disabled Veterans' Children Scholarship Board
documentation: Copy of VA disability rating letter
Veteran parent's DD214 or service/death record
findings.sourceExcerpt: "Disabled" means having a sixty per cent or greater service-connected disability or receiving benefits for permanent and total nonservice-connected disability, as determined by the United States department of veterans affairs.

findings.name: Veteran's Preference in State Civil Service Examinations
findings.description: Honorably discharged veterans, and certain reserve component members who complete initial entry training, applying for Ohio civil service positions receive additional credit added to their competitive examination score, improving their rank on the eligible list. The statute does not establish a separate or enhanced preference tier specifically for disabled veterans beyond this standard credit.
findings.value: 20% additional credit added to civil service exam score (or 15% for qualifying reserve component members with no wartime/qualifying service; the two credits are mutually exclusive)
otherReqs: Honorable discharge from the uniformed services, or reserve-component transfer with satisfactory service evidence
Ohio residency
findings.sourceExcerpt: receive additional credit of twenty per cent of the person's total grade given in the examination

findings.name: Veterans with Disabilities License Plates
findings.description: Ohio veterans with a service-connected disability rated or compensated at 100% by the VA, or who received a VA monetary allowance toward a vehicle purchase, may register a vehicle with Veterans with Disabilities plates. The first such vehicle registration is exempt from registration and service fees, and the plates permit use of parking spaces marked with the international symbol of access.
findings.value: No additional plate fee; first vehicle's registration and service fees waived entirely under ORC 4503.41
otherReqs: VA letter confirming 100% service-connected disability rating dated within the past year, OR proof of a VA monetary allowance for vehicle purchase due to service-connected disability
Fee waiver applies only to the veteran's first registered vehicle
documentation: BMV 4507 Registration Application for Gratis and Free Military License Plates
Ohio Certificate of Title or Memorandum of Title (for new vehicles)
findings.sourceExcerpt: Has a service-connected disability that is either rated or compensated at 100% from the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs.

findings.name: Free Hunting and Fishing Licenses for Disabled Veterans
findings.description: Ohio residents determined by the VA to be permanently and totally disabled, and who receive VA pension or compensation (or who hold Ohio's disabled-veteran special license plates), can receive free fishing, hunting, fur taker, deer/wild turkey, and wetlands habitat licenses and permits on an annual, multi-year, or lifetime basis as set by the Division of Wildlife.
findings.value: Free fishing/hunting license and related permits (annual, multi-year, or lifetime, per ODNR Division of Wildlife)
otherReqs: Honorable discharge from the U.S. Armed Forces
Receiving VA pension or compensation
Alternatively, holds Ohio disabled-veteran special license plates issued under ORC 4503.41
findings.agency: Ohio Department of Natural Resources, Division of Wildlife
findings.form: Disabled Veterans & Former POWs 5-Year Free License Application (DNR 9032-B)
documentation: VA determination of permanent and total disability
findings.sourceExcerpt: Every resident of this state with a disability that has been determined by the veterans administration to be permanently and totally disabling

findings.name: Ohio Veterans Bonus
findings.description: A one-time state bonus payment for Ohio veterans (or eligible survivors) who served honorably during the Global War on Terror era. This research could not directly confirm the exact current dollar amounts or full eligibility text because the administering pages (dvs.ohio.gov and apps.dvs.ohio.gov) blocked automated retrieval on every attempt in this session; figures reported by secondary sources are therefore omitted rather than presented as fact.
otherReqs: Ohio residency at time of entry to active duty and at time of application (per secondary sources, not independently confirmed)
Honorable service of 90+ days on or after October 7, 2001 (per secondary sources, not independently confirmed)
